source.authors: Wikenros C, Jarnemo A, Frisén M, Kuijper DPJ, Schmidt K
source.title: Mesopredator behavioral response to olfactory signals of an apex predator

value: red foxes visited sites with lynx scat more often than expected and their visits were longer than at control sites (no scat added)
units: categorical (visits recorded at lynx-scat sites versus control sites, chi-square goodness-of-fit against equal visitation)
method: video camera-trap field experiment: lynx (Lynx lynx) scats placed in the centre of the detection area of the camera at 27 of 54 sites, locations randomly assigned as scat site or control site (no scat added); each site monitored 12 consecutive days; visits within a 5-min interval assumed to be the same individual; visitation frequency tested with a chi-square goodness-of-fit test and visit duration with a t-test
conditions: wild-sourced: free-ranging red foxes in Bialowieza Primeval Forest, Poland (temperate mixed lowland forest, 600 km2 of it in Poland); lynx scats from two captive mature female lynx outside the mating season, kept frozen at -20 C for a few days up to 1 month; experiments started 9, 12 and 24 October and 9 November 2012 (autumn); 102 fox visits recorded, 75 at 17 scat sites and 27 at 11 control sites (so only 17 of 27 scat sites and 11 of 27 control sites were visited), chi-square = 22.59, df = 1, p < 0.0001 if equal visitation expected; the reader summary of the paper also gives visit duration 31 +/- 4 s at scat sites against 2 +/- 0.4 s at controls (t = -7.446, p < 0.001); logistic regressions scat versus control: vigilance, sniffing and scent marking more frequent at scat sites (odds ratios 22.1, 110.8 and 26.1) while passing by was more common at control sites (OR 0.019); contrary and null secondary results: vigilance was the only behaviour influenced by time since the experiment started, with foxes more vigilant when the scats were fresher (the reader summary gives OR 0.85, p = 0.058 and no significant time effect on passing by, sniffing or scent marking); prior fox over-marking of the scat raised sniffing and scent marking; marten, badger and raccoon dog visits were too few to analyse; individual foxes were not identified so visits are not independent samples; the only control is no scat added, with no non-predator scat control, so the response cannot be separated from a response to any novel scat
quote: Red fox visited sites with scats more often than expected and the duration of their visits was longer at scat sites than at control sites (no scat added).
note: Classification: behavioural_response, visitation and visit duration of wild foxes at predator-scat sites versus no-scat control sites; the value is limited to the quoted Abstract sentence and the statistics, behaviour odds ratios and nulls are carried in conditions. Byline as printed: Camilla Wikenros, Anders Jarnemo, Marielle Frisen, Dries P. J. Kuijper, Krzysztof Schmidt; DOI 10.1007/s10164-016-0504-6 printed on the page. Reached with the unfiltered WebSearch 'mdpi Animals free-ranging wild response to scent marks field trial camera traps odour stimulus control sample sites' (also returned by 'nature.com Scientific Reports wild mammals scent marking field experiment conspecific odour response camera trap latrine'), which returned link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s10164-016-0504-6.pdf. The WebFetch reader returns about 125 characters per chunk, so the quote is assembled from two consecutive chunks of Abstract sentence 3. Name: Vulpes vulpes (Linnaeus, 1758), Carnivora, Canidae on the Mammal Diversity Database page mammaldiversity.org/taxon/1005977 (opened, reached by the WebSearch 'mammaldiversity.org Vulpes vulpes red fox Canidae Carnivora'; the page prints no class, Mammalia is from the main row for the species). source.authors: Wagner CM, Bals JD, Byford GJ, Scott AM, Feder ME
source.title: Olfactory sensitivity and threat-sensitive responses to alarm cue in an invasive fish

value: conspecific alarm cue was strongly repellent in the half-channel field experiment: migrants moved upstream along the side of the channel opposite the point of odour introduction (F5,16 = 29.65, P < 0.001)
units: categorical (side of channel used by upstream-migrating females, ANOVA across cue concentrations on trial-level proportions)
method: in-stream half-channel experiment: an 8 m stream section divided into two equal-width channels by a temporary barrier; alarm cue (whole-carcass extract) pumped into one half at 75 ml per min at 0.1, 0.2 or 1.0 ul per L (a solvent control at 0), an equal volume of extraction solvent and river water pumped into the other half; 40 PIT-tagged females per trial (two holding cages of 20); four fixed PIT antennas recorded the side used; stimulus side alternated across replicates
conditions: wild-sourced: actively migrating sea lamprey trapped at dams by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service in Lake Huron and Lake Michigan tributaries, monitored at least 48 h before use, each individual used once; this experiment run in the Ocqueoc River, Michigan, 31 May to 20 June 2012; 16 trials (4 per treatment) with 640 individual females; at 0.2 and 1.0 ul per L, 93.8% (122 of 130 subjects) and 99.2% (121 of 122 subjects) of migrants avoided the cue side while continuing upstream; Tukey tests separated those two concentrations from 0.1 ul per L and the solvent control, so 0.1 ul per L did not differ from control in side choice; contrary and null secondary results: the cue had no effect on the proportion of animals swimming upstream (F3,16 = 1.14, P = 0.38); swim-up time differed across concentrations (Kruskal-Wallis chi-square = 202.03, P < 0.0001, with evidence for faster upstream movement at 0.1 ul per L and a median 40.92 min delay at 1.0 ul per L); in the companion full-channel field experiment (no cue-free side) there was no side preference (F3,16 = 0.49, P = 0.73) and only the 1.0 ul per L treatment delayed swim-up; water temperature and discharge had no effect on upstream migration; the paper's laboratory choice experiment and electro-olfactogram recordings are separate experiments not logged here; stimulus is a carcass solvent extract, so the active compound is not identified
where: Results, half-channel field experiment (Experiment 2), channel selection
quote: The alarm cue had a strong repellent effect (F5, 16=29.65, P<0.001), causing migrants to move upstream along the side of the channel opposite to the point of odor introduction.
note: Classification: behavioural_response, side choice of wild migrating sea lampreys in an in-stream half-channel with alarm cue against a solvent-and-river-water control; the value is limited to the quoted Results sentence and the percentages, Tukey result and nulls are carried in conditions.
